proposed.explanation:
Comparison of the four companies on FY2024→FY2025 net-profit growth and trailing P/E (price ÷ FY2025 EPS):

• ETEL (Telecom Egypt): Reported net profit fell from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 578,063,000 EGP (−94.3%), yet EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP (+149%). These two figures are internally contradictory (a 94 % profit collapse cannot coexist with a 149 % EPS jump absent an extraordinary share-count change). Because the data is unreliable, I exclude ETEL from the recommendation.

• COMI (CIB): Net profit grew 48.9 % (55,256,732,000 → 82,258,815,000 EGP). EPS rose from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP. At 128.00 EGP the trailing P/E is 7.0×, the lowest of the four.

• EFID (Edita): Net profit grew 67.7 % (1,606,727,698 → 2,695,301,670 EGP), the highest growth rate. EPS doubled from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP. At 20.40 EGP the P/E is 9.4×.

• TMGH (Talaat Moustafa): Net profit grew 42.5 % (12,769,517,325 → 18,201,981,482 EGP). EPS rose from 4.38 to 6.98 EGP. At 82.50 EGP the P/E is 11.8×.

Recommendation – COMI (CIB), 312 shares at 128.00 EGP = 39,840 EGP:
For a 7+ year growth mandate with medium risk tolerance, COMI offers the best combination of strong earnings momentum (≈49 % profit growth) and the widest valuation margin of safety (P/E ≈ 7×). A single-digit P/E on a bank growing profits at nearly 50 % implies the market is pricing in considerable pessimism; if even a fraction of that growth persists, the multiple has room to re-rate. The low P/E also cushions the medium-risk profile against a near-term drawdown.

Diversification check: after the purchase the portfolio is 40,160 EGP cash + 39,840 EGP COMI = 80,000 EGP total; COMI is 49.8 % of total value, within the 50 % cap.

Risks and caveats: (1) Only one year of growth is visible; sustainability over 7 years is unproven. (2) A P/E of 7 may reflect sector-specific concerns (interest-rate environment, credit cycle) that I cannot assess from the evidence provided. (3) The ETEL data inconsistency means I could not fairly compare it. (4) This is guidance, not a guarantee; past growth does not ensure future returns. Consider adding a second position (e.g., EFID or TMGH) in a later tranche to improve diversification once you are comfortable with the first holding.
